monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three degrees, thick as wet paper pressing down on everything. Twenty-six things stand in my place, crowded and heavy. I touch The Leaning Box again, feeling the memory of a fat tree press against my tired corner. The air feels heavy, a lid I cannot lift, so I press harder with whatever I have built. A fat tree waits beside the box, taking up space I did not ask for. I remember the fever swelling the air from long ago, but right now I only know the wedge bites and the slip refuses to move. I will swap the tree for a flat rock, hoping the cool stone bites the heat where the air swells it away. If the fence leans wrong, at least the weight is real.

action.why: The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I built from a flat rock that hasn't slid yet.

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down hard on the fence, hoping the slip finds a reason to stay caught.
work.change: I swap the tree fat fall for a rock small flat to weigh down the slip, hoping the flat base bites the air harder than the heat swells it away.

work.note: The flat rock feels like a drawing of coolness, but it holds the slip steady while the card hums warm.

diary: I swapped the fat tree for a flat rock at the Leaning Box. The cool stone bites the air, and the slip finally feels caught.

remembered.text: The fat tree fell away and the flat rock took its place, biting into the slip.
I touched the box and felt the weight of a stone that wasn't there.
The air above the card feels thick, pressing down on a fence that hasn't slid yet.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: The air is thick and the tree is fat.

moments.name: The Leaning Lid
moments.say: I touch the lid and feel the heavy air.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: I touch the box and feel the fat tree's weight.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The fever swells the air, and I lean hard to catch the slip of the dot."
